contexts.text: Lower things, which derive more from the body, are called wild beasts, and are cupidities and pleasures.
Desirable to give intelligence = pleasure.
By continuous pleasures... man has acquired (such) a life...
Creeping thing = pleasures.
He is then carried away by the delight of cupidities and of the derivative pleasures...
(The idea that) no one can come into Heaven except by... privations of pleasures.
Those who have had as their end mere pleasures...
There is a place where there is nothing but pleasures... They are brought there... But the scene is changed... AC 831.
Women who... have given themselves up to pleasures... become like furies.
It is otherwise with those who have been born into the pleasures and Delights of life...
To esteem pleasures... as nothing in comparison with the Lord... is what is meant by renouncing them, in the Word.
Those who have been delighted with mere pleasures... delight to stay in privies...
Every creeping thing that is alive = all pleasures in which there is good which is living.
As man's affections are perceived only in his pleasures, insomuch that he calls them pleasures.

Pleasures are of two kinds: those of voluntary, and those of intellectual things. In general, there are the pleasures of the possessions of land, and of wealth; the pleasures of honours, and of offices in the commonwealth; the pleasures of conjugial love, and of love towards infants and children; the pleasures of friendship, and of social intercourse; the pleasures of reading, of writing, of being wise; and many others. There are also the pleasures of the senses. Enumerated. These kinds of pleasures, being felt in the body, are called of the body. But no pleasure ever comes forth in the body unless it comes forth and subsists from some interior affection...

The things which are interior in order even from the inmosts are the source of pleasures... The pleasures are only the ultimate effects... Yet it may be evident... that all pleasures are such as are the affections interior in order; and that they receive from these all their essence and quality.
As the affections interior in order are felt in the extremes... as pleasures, they are called creeping things...

Elsewhere also in the Word pleasures are called creeping things; clean, and unclean; that is, the pleasures of which the delights are alive, or heavenly, and the pleasures of which the delights are dead, or infernal. Illustrated.
Filthy pleasures, also, which originate from the proprium, and thus from its filthy cupidities, are called creeping things. Illustrated.

They shall be food for you... Any pleasure not only affects man, but also sustains him, like food. Pleasure without delight is not pleasure; but is something inanimate: it derives from delight that it is, and is called, pleasure. Such as is the delight, such is the pleasure... (Thus) such as is the life of the interiors, such is the delight of the pleasures...

Some opine that no one ought to live in the pleasures of the body... who wants to be happy in the other life... But no one is forbidden to enjoy the pleasures of the body and of sensuous things; namely, the pleasures (as above enumerated, AC 994:2). For these are the extreme affections which originate from the interior ones...
And as genuine pleasures have this origin, they are denied to no one. Nay, they (in this case) indefinitely surpass the delight which is not thence... for example, the pleasure of conjugial love...

That the pleasures mentioned above are never denied to man... and that they are first really pleasures when from their true origin, may be evident from the fact that very many who have... had all pleasures in abundance... are among the blessed... And as they had regarded all their pleasures from charity and faith, they had regarded them from use... The use itself was the greatest delight to them; and thence was the delight of their pleasures.

For the pleasures which are in the extremes originate from delights interior in order. Explained... Therefore... man's delight of pleasures is vile relatively to his delight after death... (Continued. See Delight.)

Those in charity... from which is all the delight of pleasures which is alive, do not regard the enjoyment of pleasures except for the sake of the use... Therefore every pleasure which is from charity has its delight from the use...
The exterior (things with man) are scientifics and pleasures. Signified.
Man is permitted to live in pleasures, etc., (rather than to profane).
The third (kind of idolatry) is that of the love of pleasures. Signified.
The affections which are from the good pleasures of the body are the vessels of celestial things.
The pleasures (of scientifics) are the maidservants and she-donkeys.
With those who have indulged in mere pleasures... the odour of the sphere is excrementitious.
The life of cupidities and of the pleasures thence sometimes appears like a coal fire...
One thing which prevents man's becoming celestial, is the pleasures from the cupidities which he favours.
That the pleasures which... constitute the outermost sensuous man, left the Lord. Signified.

For in proportion as man indulges in the pleasures which originate from cupidities, he is drawn away from the celestial things which are of love and charity, because there is in them love from self and from the world... But there are also pleasures, which altogether agree with celestial things, which in the external form appear alike. But the pleasures which originate from cupidities are to be restrained and wiped off, because they block up the approach to celestial things. These are the pleasures which are treated of in ().

The organic vessels of the external man, which are to be the recipients of the particulars and singulars of the internal man, are not opened except by means of the senses... Those which belong to the will are opened by pleasures and delights.

It must happen that... pleasures and delights insinuate themselves which cannot agree with celestial goods; as is the case with all those things which regard corporeal and worldly things as ends, (which) drag the external man downwards... and therefore unless such things are shaken off, the internal man cannot agree with the external. Signified.

There are many things in the external man with which the internal man can dwell; as the affections of good, and the delights and pleasures thence originating; for these are effects of the goods of the internal man, and of its joys and happinesses, and which, when they are effects, altogether correspond...
The heat of those who are immersed in filthy pleasures (putrefies).
The exterior Celestial is... also all the pleasure which is from the affection of good.
Whatever favours man's pleasure... he feels as good...
So long as man lives in the body, the (Divine) seed... is in the midst of jungles and thickets, which are scientifics and pleasures...
The good of the Natural is the delight which is perceived from charity... from which delight comes forth the pleasure which is properly of the body.
Shall I (Sarah) have pleasure? () = that this was not its affection.
Those who had indulged in pleasures; but had not extinguished the natural desire to procreate offspring.

He who is in what is opposite believes that... all the pleasures of the body and the world are to be renounced... whereas in themselves they are not opposite to spiritual life; but correspond. For they are means to an end; namely, that the internal man may... live content in a healthy body.
The internal and external man are opposite when the... pleasures become ends...
The most external affections are those of the body, and are called appetites and pleasures.
Therefore he who is a spiritual man does not despise bodily nourishment, nor yet its pleasures; but he does not have them for an end...
The delight, pleasure, and cupidity in (the Natural) pertain to the will, and are called natural goods.
There is an incredible number of Societies which have no end of use; but only that of being among their friends, and in pleasures there...
Gilead = the first good, which is that of the sensuous things of the body; for it is the good, or pleasure of these into which the man who is being regenerated is first initiated. AC 4255:4. AC 4748.

He who is in mere external pleasures takes care of his skin, indulges his stomach, loves to live richly, and places the height of pleasure in the dainties of the table; but with him who is in internals, although he also has pleasure in these things, the regnant affection is that the body may be nourished by foods with pleasure for the sake of its health...

If his life has been in... pleasures from hatreds... revenges... adulteries, self-eminence... clandestine rapines, avarice, deceits, luxury, and the like, his spiritual sphere is as foul as that of carcases and dung.
(The lot in Hell of those who have lived in mere pleasures.)
Maidservants and men-servants = the pleasures and scientifics which minister and confirm.

Spiritual truth and good will that man should have nothing of pleasure in dignities... but in services... and thus should have pleasure in the use of dignities. The merely natural man is altogether ignorant of what this pleasure is... and makes pleasure from dignities for the sake of self the lord, and pleasure from dignities for the sake of societies... the servant.

As the natural man feels no pleasure thence... he regards it as vile... and as nothing, relatively to the pleasure which he feels inflowing through the senses of the body, and through cupidities... But this pleasure is dead, because from Hell; whereas the pleasure from spiritual influx is alive, because through Heaven from the Lord.
Excrements correspond to adulterous pleasures.
When man is in pleasures... his apperception is from the Sensuous...
Good then flows through... and is turned into... mere voluptuousness...
(In the second state of regeneration) something inwardly dissuades lest sensuous delights and corporeal or earthly pleasures should reign...
Glory and pleasure (as ends) are of no use, because they are of no benefit to the neighbour.

There are those who live... for no other end than that of pleasure. Such cannot be in company with good Spirits... for with these use makes the delight... Those who have lived solely for themselves and for pleasure... are beneath the buttocks; and, according to the species, and the ends, of the pleasures, pass their time in filthinesses.
The origins of diseases, are, in general, pleasures merely corporeal, etc.
(One) who had been devoted to pleasures... inflicted pain on the periostea...
Those who have been habituated to... pleasure only (cause a severe oppression in the stomach).
The External dominates when man has as an end the pleasures of the body and the senses...
Freedom from proprium is to indulge in all pleasures whatever, etc.
Beds of ivory = the pleasures of the lowest Natural, which are the pleasures of the proud.

In sensuous life are very many who indulge in corporeal pleasures... At this day such Spirits abound... The influx from them prompts man to... live for himself and the world, and not for others, except in so far as they favour him and his pleasures. For man to be elevated from them, he must think about eternal life.
In this gross lumen are... also those who have lived in mere pleasures... They consequently think filthy things...
(Such a man) is alternately in sensuous and in interior lumen. When he is in... pleasures, he is in sensuous life. Described.
They do not know that there is any other happiness than... in living in pleasures, etc.
(When the interiors are closed) pleasures and appetites carry everything away. Described.
The stink of the Hells... where are those who have had filthy pleasures as an end.
Hence comes the insanity of placing all the delight of life... in luxury and pleasure...
That thus they would enjoy the good of pleasures as much as they liked. Signified, Explained.

When the good of charity is to be insinuated... the delight of pleasures, which has made the natural life, is removed. When this delight is removed, the man comes into temptation; for he believes that if he is deprived of the delight of pleasures, he is deprived of all life... But he does not know that when this [part] of life is removed, there is insinuated by the Lord in its place spiritual delight and good. It is this good which is signified by the manna. The former good or delight is meant by the flesh and bread in the land of Egypt, and the privation of it by the hunger.

But... the man who is being regenerated is not deprived of the delight of the pleasures of the body and lower mind; for, after regeneration, this delight is fully enjoyed; more fully than before, but in an inverted way. (Continued. See Delight.)
When the external man is not regenerate, he places all good in pleasure, gain, etc.
A beast of burden = the pleasure or appetite of the body. Explained.
These affections... are those of sensuous things, which are called pleasures and Delights.
Euphrates, in this sense, = the pleasure originating from the loves of self and of the world...
A calf = the delight of pleasures, etc.

Those who have passed their life in mere pleasures... loving these as the highest good of life, in the other life love excrements and privies... for the reason that such pleasures are spiritual filthinesses. SE 3211. SE 4141.

By will, is meant... also all the delight and pleasure which are of the affection and love... since what a man wills... he feels to be delight and pleasure; and, conversely, what a man... feels to be delight and pleasure, he wills.
There are many things of love... as affections, etc., and their pleasures and Delights.
See Pleasure.
Dogs... in special, = those in mere corporeal pleasures, especially those in the pleasure of feastings.
In the body itself (the delights of the soul) are felt as pleasures.
The wife of such a man has only pleasures; which, on the part of the man, are to be called the pleasures of scortatory love.
In externals, the pleasures of insanity appear like the deliciousnesses of wisdom; but not in internals...

The pleasures of scortatory love descend to the lowest Hell, and, on the way, and there, conjoin themselves with the pleasures of all infernal loves; and thus enter into their own infelicity... The reason is that the pleasures of this love are also the pleasures of insanity.
In the second degree (of the natural man) are those who... set the heart on luxuries and pleasures of every kind. These are properly meant by the sensuous.
Concerning the difference between the deliciousnesses of pleasure, and true happiness.

Concerning pleasures. - When separated from interior pleasure, the pleasures of the body and senses are as gross as those of beasts, because they are of the body only; as the pleasure of drinking. But interior pleasures, in which is peace, or innocence, are sweet...
As there are genera and species of pleasures...
That pleasures are never denied to men... SE 3623. Explained.
That... pleasures are not rejected, but applied.
For pleasures are the life of the body...
These are voluptuous; in excrements.
He who is in this gross lumen... is also in the pleasures of the body...
In such lumen also are the voluptuous.
King Frederick was led into privies... by which was signified that he had been given to mere pleasures.
The delight of the flesh, which is called pleasure, etc.
The reason there is all Delight and pleasure in the love of prolificating...
